solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He likes a light macaroni cooked after pastry is scooped out

indicators.note: after places the cooked pasta behind the pastry remnant
a pastry case scooped out keeps only its shell, so just the outside letters of pastry remain
cooked means the letters of macaroni are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A fussy diner wants some macaroni prepared after the pastry has been hollowed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is scooped out' leaves PY, the outer letters of pastry; 'cooked' turns MACARONI into ROMANIAC. 'He likes a light' sounds like a smoker but defines a firebug.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a compulsion to start fires is cryptically a man who enjoys setting things alight.

clue.text: Lose one's temper over receiving abominable vacuous lyrics

indicators.note: receiving means the reversed word takes the next piece inside it
over in a down clue means the word for losing one's temper is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to snap is to lose one's temper

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outer letters of abominable remain

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage at hearing dreadful, empty song words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses SNAP to PANS; 'vacuous' empties abominable to AE, which PANS receives.
explanation.definitionFit: Paeans are songs of praise or triumph, so the words are lyrics of celebration.

clue.text: Land river fish by empty pub

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: empty means the word for pub loses its middle letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An angler lands a river fish next to a deserted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' means the pub word is gutted of its middle, a common cryptic convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To land a fish is to wind the line and pull the catch to shore.

clue.text: Head of house? Presumably dad's subordinate

definitions.meaning: the nun in charge of a convent, a religious house
if mum is superior, the father must rank below her; the whimsy reads the title literally

explanation.surface: Who runs the household? Presumably father plays second fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbess of a convent is styled thus; read literally, the title says mum outranks dad.

clue.text: Shelter in north is closed around end of June and November

indicators.note: around means the closed word wraps the following letters

parts.note: shut means closed

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of June

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A northern shelter is shut from late June through November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts EN inside SHUT for SENHUT. A Nissen hut is a corrugated-iron half-cylinder building from the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: This prefabricated arched hut was built to house troops, a basic military refuge.

clue.text: Answer call showing excitement

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Answering the phone with evident excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is abuzz hums with lively activity and anticipation.

clue.text: Conservative charity almost collected

indicators.note: almost means the word for charity loses its final letter

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A Tory charity has nearly finished gathering its donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S of ALMS, leaving ALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone collected is composed and unruffled, a synonym of serene.

clue.text: Drink vermouth provided after topless frolic

indicators.note: after places the vermouth and condition behind the trimmed frolic
topless means the first letter of the frolic word is dropped

parts.note: a caper is a playful frolic
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
if means provided, as a condition

explanation.surface: A drink of vermouth, so long as it follows a topless romp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts CAPER to APER. IT for Italian vermouth is a British bar convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic beverage taken before a meal to stimulate appetite.

clue.text: Behaving badly to young lady in graduation initially entertains university

indicators.note: entertains means the combined pieces hold the next letter as a guest

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of graduation

explanation.surface: A young woman at her graduation entertains the university with bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' means the university letter goes inside the run made by the young lady, in and the initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone wrongly is abusing or ill-treating them, conduct that is improper towards another.

clue.text: Even more terribly mad for opening of Bertie Wooster novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the gathered letters are made into a fresh arrangement
opening of takes the first letter of Bertie

explanation.surface: Someone is even more crazy about a P G Wodehouse book starring Bertie Wooster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges MADFOR, B and WOOSTER. Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's comic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation deteriorating further, getting still worse than it was.

clue.text: Losing head, refuse bail out

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for refuse is dropped

parts.note: to refuse something is to reject it

explanation.surface: A beheaded prisoner, it seems, is refused bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' removes the R from REJECT. 'bail out' looks like a legal phrase but is the pilot's escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail out of an aircraft is to be thrown clear of it, as an ejector seat does.

clue.text: Fighting on board, making a start to impound stores

indicators.note: on, as in on board, means being carried aboard, so the rest sits inside the vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is on board

indicators.note: making a into something else says one letter of the fight word is replaced

parts.note: a quarrel is a fight or row

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of impound is taken

explanation.surface: Sailors brawl aboard ship, and someone moves to seize the provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a start to impound' turns the A of QUARREL into I, giving QUIRREL, which goes 'on' SS, the steamship ('board').
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel things away is to hoard them for later, so it is a verb meaning to keep in reserve.

clue.text: In a vet, bats have ultimately too much trust

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters of in a vet are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of have

explanation.surface: Bats taken to a vet end up trusting him too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' rearranges INAVET to NAIVET, and 'ultimately' adds E, the last letter of have.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence that leads one to believe others too readily, an excess of credulity.

clue.text: Stupid people cross motorway by ice regularly, slipping at first

parts.note: a zo (also dzo) is a hybrid of yak and domestic cow, so a cross
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of by ice, starting with the first
at first takes the opening letter of slipping

explanation.surface: Fools cross the motorway on the ice and start slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes BIE from the letters of by ice; 'at first' gives S from slipping. 'cross' looks like a verb but is the yak-cow hybrid ZO.
explanation.definitionFit: Zombies are slang for dull, mindless people who act as if they were the walking dead.

clue.text: Continent holds difficulty for dictator suspiciously into failure of vital functions

indicators.note: holds means the continent wraps around the next piece

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: for dictator means the word is spoken out loud, as to someone taking dictation

parts.note: a fix is a difficult spot or predicament

indicators.note: suspiciously means the letters of into are viewed askew and rearranged

explanation.surface: A continent faces trouble as a dictator suspiciously slides into failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for dictator' is a homophone signal: the word is spoken as if to a secretary taking dictation, then spelt oddly. 'suspiciously' rearranges into.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocation is the body being starved of oxygen, so the life-sustaining processes give out.

clue.text: Axes cut more than 50 per cent of upright instrument

parts.note: x and y are the axes of a graph
to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: more than 50 per cent of means only the front part of the word for upright is kept, a bit beyond its first half

parts.note: an upright person is honest

explanation.surface: Axes cut through most of an upright piano-like instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than 50 per cent of' keeps four of the six letters of HONEST, not an exact half. 'Axes' looks like choppers but is graph axes.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument has wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Officer supports second pillbox perhaps

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments
a pillbox is a small round hat, so an example of a hat

explanation.surface: An officer backs a second wartime gun emplacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pillbox' looks military, a concrete bunker, but here it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is slang for a high-ranking military officer with gold braid on his cap.

clue.text: A cost cut stupidly, swapping toaster's lead for current that's not electric

indicators.note: stupidly means the letters are thrown about in a muddled order
swapping one thing out says a letter of the fodder is replaced
for names what goes in, completing the exchange of letters
lead takes the first letter of toaster's

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cost-cutting idiot swapped a toaster's flex for one that isn't electric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping … for' replaces a T in ACOSTCUT with I; 'stupidly' then rearranges ACOSICUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An acoustic guitar makes its sound without amplification, unlike a plugged-in model.

clue.text: Summarise yield again?

definitions.meaning: to summarise is to go over the main points briefly
to capitulate is to surrender; the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether summing up means giving in once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap a discussion is to restate its main points in brief; split, the word also means surrendering anew.

clue.text: K Bacon perhaps adopts student

indicators.note: adopts means the name takes in the next letter

parts.note: Kevin Bacon is an American actor, so his first name is an example
L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: K Bacon, an actor perhaps, adopts a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'K Bacon' reads as a name, but K is the definition and 'Bacon perhaps' gives KEVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol K stands for the SI unit of absolute temperature named after Lord Kelvin.

clue.text: Religious book in hotel converted many on left

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: converted means the letters of many are changed into another form

explanation.surface: A holy book in a hotel has converted many on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges MANY to YMNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of hymns sung in church is a devotional volume.

clue.text: Nearly jet south to net minute worms

indicators.note: to net means to catch, so the pieces enclose the next letter
nearly means the word for jet loses its last letter

parts.note: a squirt is a jet of liquid

explanation.surface: Someone nearly squirts a jet southward to catch tiny worms in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' trims SQUIRT to SQUIR; with S added, SQUIRS nets M. 'worms' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To worm is to wriggle or twist about, just as someone uncomfortable fidgets.

clue.text: Guru succeeded with friend

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogy
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A guru found success with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a spiritual master like an Indian guru.

clue.text: Brittle conclusion of inquiry after Democrat enters government

indicators.note: after places that last letter behind the rest
enters means the Democrat goes inside the word for government

parts.note: power is government or rule, as in the party in power

indicators.note: conclusion of takes the last letter of inquiry

explanation.surface: After an inquiry concludes, a Democrat enters a fragile government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts D inside POWER; 'conclusion of' gives Y from inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brittle crumbles easily into dust, the way a friable substance does.

clue.text: Stew a time over controversial issue

parts.note: a hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat topped with sliced potato
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A stew left simmering for a while becomes a talking point.
explanation.walkthrough: HOTPOT is a British meat and potato casserole; O for over comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter so contentious that everyone wants to drop it quickly is called by this idiom.

clue.text: Wine variety turned bottles black

indicators.note: turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
bottles means the two words hold the letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A type of wine, turned, ends up in dark bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bottles black' as the definition, but 'bottles' is the containment signal: wiNE VARiety holds NEVAR, which 'turned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Raven as an adjective describes glossy jet colouring, as in raven hair.

clue.text: Leaders in training ambassadors can teach diplomacy

indicators.note: leaders in means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Training of ambassadors is what instils diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders in' takes the initial letters of training ambassadors can teach.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitivity in handling others without giving offence is the essence of diplomatic skill.

clue.text: Seed is light red around Spain, navy in East European lake

indicators.note: around means the colour wraps the Spain letter

parts.note: pink is a pale red
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: in means the navy goes inside the following letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A seed, pinkish in colour, travels from Spain via the navy to a lake in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' and 'in' are both containment signals; E for Spain comes from international car registration plates.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible kernel from a conifer cone is used in pesto and is botanically a seed.
